newsitem.title: JAPAN: Profits jump at Japan personal loan firm Acom Co.
newsitem.headline: Profits jump at Japan personal loan firm Acom Co.

text.p: One of Japan's leading consumer finance companies, Acom Co Ltd, reported a 20 percent rise in its interim parent current profit on Tuesday and said it expects buoyant full-year profits.

"In our loan sector, we increased the number of our automatic teller machines (ATMs), built more roadside outlets and expanded our cash dispenser network by establishing ties with other financial institutions," Acom said in a statement.
A company spokeswoman said that in the six months to September 30, 1996, the firm built 294 new ATMs across Japan, bringing its total to 645.

As a result, the firm, which is in its 60th year of business, increased its outstanding loans by 17.5 percent to 918.99 billion yen compared with the same half-year period a year earlier. Interest income on the loans stood at 114.97 billion yen, up 14.7 percent.
The firm said its parent current profit was 42.42 billion yen in the half-year against 35.41 billion yen a year ago.

Analysts said the key to clientele expansion for consumer finance firms, once frowned upon as loan sharks charging outrageously high interest rates, lies in the increasing market share of ATMs, where customers can discreetly borrow money.

They added that despite the increase in borrowings, the firms were relatively safe from any damage from non-performing loans, as their loans are for individuals and not firms, and the sums are not staggering.
Japan's record-low interest rates are also a big plus for the consumer finance firms, who themselves borrow funds from financial institutions, industry sources said.

By the end of the fiscal year in March 31, 1997 the spokeswoman said the company hopes to augment the number of its ATMs to 780. As a result, the company is forecasting a parent current profit of 83.80 billion yen for the full fiscal year, against 75.54 billion a year earlier. This would be a rise of 11 percent.
Acom shares, which are listed on the first section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange, settled 10 yen higher at 4,390 yen.
